title: Standardized Testing & Education
rootClaim: Standardized testing and rigid national curricula hinder genuine intellectual development and should be replaced by student-centered, exploratory learning.

branches.text: Standardized testing reduces education to memorization, promotes 'teaching to the test', and destroys intrinsic intellectual curiosity.

children.text: Multiple-choice assessments penalize lateral, creative thinking by forcing complex real-world concepts into binary right-or-wrong metrics.
Psychometric Reliability: Standardized assessments offer objective, verifiable, and scalable evaluation across diverse demographics without subjective teacher grading bias.
Socioeconomic Confounding: Standardized scores correlate far more strongly with family income and test-prep coaching access than actual student capability or diligence.
Holistic admissions and subjective evaluations show even higher correlations with elite privilege due to un-standardized legacy network opportunities.
Exploratory Montessori/Dewey models foster critical problem-solving, self-efficacy, and adaptive passion-driven skill acquisition.

branches.text: Standardized testing is essential for maintaining academic accountability, equity benchmarks, and meritocratic resource allocation.

children.text: Signaling Model of Education: Standardized metrics provide external labor markets and universities with clear signals of cognitive discipline and persistence.
Goodhart's Law: When a measure becomes a high-stakes target (e.g., school funding tied to test scores), it ceases to be a good measure.
Adaptive computer testing (e.g., CAT) continually adjusts difficulty based on prior answers, mitigating simple test-coaching exploits.
Without standardized national benchmarks, educational disparities between underfunded and wealthy school districts remain invisible and uncorrected.

definitions.description: An adage stating that 'When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure'.
Economic theory proposing that the primary value of higher education lies in signaling pre-existing traits (intelligence, discipline) to employers rather than skill acquisition.
A student-centered learning approach based on self-directed activity, hands-on learning, and collaborative play.
The degree to which an assessment tool produces stable and consistent results across different trials and environments.
